title: Phrases
description: Learn phrases for Grade 7: noun, verb, adjective, adverb and prepositional phrases, and how a phrase differs from a clause — with bilingual notes, examples, practice and tests.

topics.title: Phrase vs Clause; Noun & Verb Phrases
topics.concept:
The simple test: a clause has a subject and a verb; a phrase does not.

  • under the old bridge → phrase (no subject-verb)
  • when the train arrived → clause (subject 'train' + verb 'arrived')

A noun phrase is a noun plus its modifiers, working as one noun:

  • The tall boy in blue won the race. (subject)

A verb phrase is the main verb with its helping verbs:

  • She has been singing. / They will have finished.

examples.problem: Phrase or clause? in the early morning
Find the verb phrase: They have been waiting for an hour.
examples.solution: have been waiting — the main verb with its helping verbs.

recap: A phrase has NO subject-verb pair; a clause does
Noun phrase = a noun plus its modifiers (the tall boy in blue)
Verb phrase = main verb + helping verbs (has been singing)

topics.title: Adjective, Adverb & Prepositional Phrases
topics.concept:
An adjective phrase describes a noun:

  • A man of great courage spoke. (describes 'man')
  • The water was cold as ice.

An adverb phrase modifies a verb, adjective or another adverb, telling how, when, where or to what degree:

  • She sang in a sweet voice. (how) / He came after some time. (when)

A prepositional phrase begins with a preposition and ends with a noun/pronoun. It very often does the job of an adjective or an adverb:

  • The book on the shelf is mine. (adjective – describes 'book')
  • He slept on the floor. (adverb – tells where)

examples.problem: Adjective or adverb phrase? The girl with red hair smiled.
examples.solution: Adjective phrase — 'with red hair' describes the noun 'girl'.

examples.problem: What does the phrase do: He ran with great speed.?
examples.solution: Adverb phrase — 'with great speed' tells how he ran.

recap: Adjective phrase describes a noun (a man of courage)
Adverb phrase tells how/when/where/to what degree
A prepositional phrase often acts as an adjective or adverb

questions.q: 'behind the door' is a:
questions.explanation: No subject-verb → phrase.

questions.q: 'will have finished' is a:
questions.explanation: Main verb + helpers → verb phrase.

questions.q: 'a girl with blue eyes' — 'with blue eyes' is a:
questions.explanation: Describes 'girl' → adjective phrase.

questions.q: 'He worked with great care.' — the phrase tells:
questions.explanation: Adverb phrase of manner (how).

questions.q: Which is a clause?
questions.explanation: 'since he came' has a subject and verb.

questions.q: 'The old man in the corner' is a:
questions.explanation: A noun with modifiers → noun phrase.

questions.q: 'She sang in a sweet voice.' — phrase type?
questions.explanation: Tells how she sang → adverb phrase.

questions.q: 'of great value' is a/an:
questions.explanation: Describes a noun → adjective phrase.

questions.q: Identify the prepositional phrase: 'The dog ran across the road.'
questions.explanation: 'across the road' begins with a preposition.

questions.q: 'has been playing' — head word?
questions.explanation: The main verb 'playing' is the head.

questions.q: Which group has NO subject-verb pair?
questions.explanation: 'in the morning' is a phrase.

questions.q: 'A man of words and not of deeds' uses which phrase type?
questions.explanation: 'of words', 'of deeds' describe the noun 'man'.

questions.q: Identify the function: 'The decision to leave early surprised us.'
options: 'to leave early' is an adjective phrase (describes 'decision')
questions.explanation: The infinitive phrase 'to leave early' modifies the noun 'decision'.

questions.q: Which sentence replaces a clause with an equivalent phrase correctly? 'Because he was honest, he was trusted.'
options: On account of his honesty, he was trusted.
He was honest, he was trusted.
Honest he was, trusted he was.
questions.explanation: The adverb clause becomes the prepositional phrase 'On account of his honesty'.

questions.q: Spot the error: 'He is a man with a great determination.'
questions.explanation: The set phrase is 'of great determination' or 'with great determination' (no article).

questions.q: Identify the head word of the phrase 'extremely difficult indeed'.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'difficult' is the head of this adjective phrase.

questions.q: Which underlined group is a noun phrase acting as an object? 'I admire (her great patience).'
questions.explanation: 'her great patience' is a noun phrase, the object of 'admire'.

questions.q: Convert the phrase to a clause: 'On reaching home, she rested.'
options: When she reached home, she rested.
questions.explanation: The phrase 'On reaching home' becomes the clause 'When she reached home'.

questions.q: Rearrange into a sentence with an adjective phrase: 'courage / a / of / great / man / spoke'
options: A man of great courage spoke.
A great courage of man spoke.
Of great courage a man spoke.
A man great of courage spoke.
questions.explanation: 'of great courage' is the adjective phrase describing 'man'.

questions.q: Which sentence contains BOTH a phrase and a clause?
options: In the morning, when the sun rose, the birds sang.
questions.explanation: 'In the morning' is a phrase; 'when the sun rose' is a clause.

outcomes: Define a phrase and tell it apart from a clause
Identify noun, verb, adjective and adverb phrases
Recognise prepositional phrases and their function
Use phrases to add detail to a sentence
Spot the head word of a phrase

intro.en: A phrase is a group of words that work together but have no subject-and-verb pair. That is the key difference from a clause. A phrase adds detail and is named after its main word — a noun phrase, a verb phrase, and so on.
intro.hi: वाक्यांश (phrase) शब्दों का वह समूह है जो साथ मिलकर काम करते हैं पर जिसमें कर्ता-क्रिया का जोड़ा नहीं होता। यही उपवाक्य (clause) से इसका मुख्य अंतर है। वाक्यांश ब्योरा जोड़ता है और अपने मुख्य शब्द के नाम पर कहलाता है — noun phrase, verb phrase, आदि।

real_life.situation:
You describe a scene:

You: The tall boy in the blue shirt ran across the field very quickly.
real_life.why: 'The tall boy in the blue shirt' is a noun phrase (who), 'across the field' is a prepositional/adverb phrase (where), and 'very quickly' is an adverb phrase (how). None of these has its own subject-verb — they are phrases, not clauses.

reading.passage: In the middle of the forest, a small wooden cabin stood quietly. A man of great wisdom lived there. Every evening, with a cup of tea in his hand, he would sit on the old porch and watch the setting sun. People from distant villages came to seek his advice.

questions.q: Find a prepositional phrase that tells 'where'.
questions.answer: "In the middle of the forest" (also 'on the old porch') — an adverbial prepositional phrase of place.

questions.q: Find an adjective phrase describing a person.
Identify a noun phrase from the passage.
questions.answer: "a small wooden cabin" (also 'a man of great wisdom') — a noun with its modifiers.

writing.prompt: Write five sentences, each containing a different phrase: a noun phrase, a verb phrase, an adjective phrase, an adverb phrase and a prepositional phrase.
writing.example: The tall girl in green won. She has been practising hard. A boy of great talent sang. He left after a while. The ball rolled under the car.

micro_quiz.explanation: Main verb + helping verbs → verb phrase.

micro_quiz.q: 'a man of honour' — the phrase 'of honour' is:
'He spoke in a loud voice.' — 'in a loud voice' is:
micro_quiz.explanation: It tells how he spoke → adverb phrase.

micro_quiz.q: Which is a clause, not a phrase?
micro_quiz.explanation: 'when it rained' has a subject and verb.

challenge.q: Identify the function of 'on the hill': 'The house on the hill is old.'
challenge.explanation: It describes the noun 'house', so it works as an adjective phrase.

challenge.q: Which group is NOT a phrase?
challenge.explanation: 'although he tried' has a subject and verb → it is a clause.

challenge.q: Replace the clause with a phrase: 'When the sun set, we left.'
options: Because the sun set, we left.
After the sun had set, we left.
challenge.explanation: 'At sunset' is a phrase that replaces the time clause.

revision: A phrase is a word group with no subject-verb pair
Named after its head word: noun, verb, adjective, adverb, prepositional
A verb phrase = main verb + helping verbs (has been working)
Prepositional phrases often act as adjectives or adverbs
Test: subject + verb = clause; otherwise it's a phrase
